description: We are a team of passionate students interested in space exploration, coding, and innovation. We aim to use NASA's open data to develop creative solutions and make a difference through teamwork and technology.
summary: MarsPath is an interactive, layered map of Jezero Crater that helps plan a safe human surface excursion (a Marswalk). It combines three kinds of NASA and USGS data: topography (HiRISE digital terrain model), optical imagery (CTX orthoimage) and geologic units (USGS geologic map). From the elevation model we derive slope, hillshade and hazard zones (caution 15 to 25 degrees, no-go above 25 degrees). We then use the A* algorithm to plan a route from the habitat at the Perseverance landing site to the Western Delta: 7.4 km, about 2.5 hours at 3 km/h, with a maximum slope of 15 degrees, inside an 8 km emergency return radius. The Western Inflow Channel, about 10 km further, is marked as a rover-supported trip. A crew safety panel summarises terrain limits, the return radius, a radiation reference value and a dust note. The map shows astronauts where to walk, what terrain and rock they will reach, and how to get back safely.
details:
Problem: Regional and global Mars maps are not detailed enough for a single Marswalk. Astronauts need to know which route is safe, how far they can go, and how to return.

What it does: MarsPath is a layered interactive map of Jezero Crater with an optical image (CTX), geologic units (USGS), slope, elevation, hillshade, caution and no-go zones, an on-foot route, a rover-supported route, an 8 km return radius, science stops with popups, and a crew safety panel.

How it works: (1) Load the HiRISE DTM and downsample it to a 20 m grid. (2) Compute slope and a cost map (above 15 degrees costs more, above 25 degrees is blocked). (3) Plan routes with the A* algorithm. (4) Align the CTX image and the geologic polygons to the DTM grid. (5) Build the Folium map with layer toggles.

Results: Habitat to Western Delta (on foot) is 7.4 km, about 2.5 hours at 3 km/h, maximum slope 15 degrees. Western Delta to Western Inflow Channel (rover-supported) is 10.2 km. 6.7% of the mapped area is caution terrain and 0.6% is no-go terrain.

Assumptions and limitations: The slope limits, walking speed and 8 km return radius are our assumptions. The geologic map was made on a different CTX base, so its alignment with our optical layer is approximate. The Western Inflow Channel position is approximate. The radiation value is a Curiosity reference, not measured at Jezero. No thermal or spectral layer yet.

Tools: Python, Google Colab, rasterio, GeoPandas, scikit-image, Folium, GitHub.

Code: https://github.com/25243060-creator/martian-map-route-planner

AI assistance: We used an AI assistant (Claude by Anthropic) to help write and debug code, draft text, and design the title slide of our demo video. Our team selected the data, ran the analysis and checked the results.
